title: Video courses for 300,000 students
summary: CursosMX sells recorded courses to 300,000 students in Mexico and Central America. Videos must arrive fast, raw recordings must cost little, and the login receives SQL injection attempts.

requirements.1: {{s1}} answers from the region the most requested pages and images, without the request reaching the servers; it does not keep files larger than 100 MB.
requirements.2: {{s2}} delivers millions of videos that students watch every day directly over the internet; you pay per stored GB and there are no servers to manage.
requirements.3: {{s3}} keeps the raw recordings for 5 years, and they are almost never opened. What matters is the lowest cost per stored GB, even if reading them later costs more or takes longer.
requirements.4: {{s4}} holds the records for cursosmx.com and answers anyone on the internet who asks for that name, so they reach the entry in Querétaro.
requirements.5: {{s5}} checks every HTTP request to the login and blocks SQL injection before it reaches the app.
requirements.6: The load balancer backend set spreads what the cache did not answer, such as login and payments, across the servers in the region.

s1.explanation: Web Application Acceleration is a policy assigned to an HTTP load balancer that caches 200 responses to GET and HEAD to spare the servers; the cache holds 100 MB and does not keep larger files.
s1.hint_cue: without the request reaching the servers

s2.explanation: Object Storage stores unstructured data of any content type, such as videos, and lets you read it directly from the internet; it is a regional service not tied to any Compute instance.

s3.explanation: The Archive tier has the lowest Object Storage cost and a 90-day minimum; each object is restored before it can be read, which takes up to an hour.
s3.hint_cue: the lowest cost per stored GB

s4.explanation: An OCI DNS internet zone answers anyone who queries it. A private zone has similar capabilities, but only answers clients that reach it through a VCN.

s5.explanation: The OCI WAF policy is regional and works as a plug-in for the load balancer; it creates rules against SQL injection, XSS and other OWASP vulnerabilities.

oci-block-volume.s2: A Block Volume attaches to an instance over iSCSI and the instance uses it like a hard drive; the video origin must be read directly from the internet.
oci-block-volume.s3: A Block Volume is block storage for an instance, not one of the Object Storage tiers.

oci-object-storage-ia.s3: Infrequent Access costs less than Standard, but it is not the cheapest tier, and it charges for every GB read.
oci-object-storage-ia.s2: Infrequent Access charges for every GB read and requires 31 days minimum; it does not suit videos watched every day.

oci-dns-private.s4: A private zone only answers clients that reach it through a VCN; students on the internet cannot query it.

oci-nsg.s5: NSG rules allow traffic by direction, IP protocol, ports and source or destination; the rules against SQL injection belong to another service.

oci-cache.s1: OCI Cache builds in-memory clusters for applications and is reached only through a private endpoint; students on the internet cannot get to it.
oci-cache.s2: OCI Cache is in-memory storage for applications, reached through a private endpoint; it does not deliver videos directly over the internet.
